text:
maya: Heads-up — during yesterday's canary bring-up for magnet13b-int4 we observed a reproducible recall dip for long-context prompts after the rollforward snapshot. attaching quick notes and a tiny reproducer.

sam: Ugh. Details? numbers? :eyes:

maya: Short version: 2.5% drop in top-5 recall on our longcontext benchmark (8k tokens) after the rollforward that included the `kv_prefill` refactor + new rotary scaling. Small prompt that fails: long-story-with-anchors.txt (I'll paste later). Repro steps below.

aisha: Do we know if it's kv index alignment vs RoPE scale mismatch? Those usually look similar in signals.

maya: Initial hypothesis: mismatch between snapshotting sequence offsets (deckchair snapshots) and new rotary phase normalization -> leads to subtle token phase slips when rehydrating KV for long runs.

ravi: Fancy name "deckchair" :grin: How confident are we it's the rollforward and not quantization noise from int4 kernels?

maya: Confidence moderate. We rolled back to previous snapshot (pre-refactor) with same int4 artifacts and recall reverts. Also two small diffs in the snapshot metadata: `prefill_stride` changed and `rotary_scale` floor shifted from 1e-2 -> 1e-3.

sam: Can you paste the tiny repro and the eval command? I can run locally on my dev rig.

maya: Reproducer (use dev image rwinf/dev:canary):

```
# run short eval
python eval/run_longctx.py \
  --model magnet13b-int4 --snapshot s-2026-03-19-deckchair \
  --prompt tests/long-story-with-anchors.txt --max-tokens 8192 \
  --kvcache-mode resume --seed 42 --emit-json
```

Outputs: baseline top5: 0.882, canary top5: 0.858. Diff ~0.024 (2.4%). Also see this excerpt from logits diff (trimmed):

```
LOGITS_DIFF_SUMMARY: {"prefill_region_mismatch": 0.0021, "rotary_phase_shift_mean": 0.00087}
```

aisha: That `rotary_phase_shift_mean` caught my eye. Did the refactor change how we compute rotational phase for wraparound indices? I remember an optimization that precomputes scale per shard.

maya: Yes. New code does per-shard normalization at snapshot creation time instead of at runtime. That was intended to reduce compute but may have introduced a rounding mismatch under quantized accumulation.

ravi: Quick idea: run a "rehydrate-check" that computes per-token expected phase vs stored phase and fails if L2 > eps. I can throw a quick script together.

sam: I'll run the repro with the flag `--force-legacy-rotary` and `--kvcache-stride 64` to see if it mitigates. If it does, it's likely rotary normalization change.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy s-2026-03-19-deckchair rolled to 3% of traffic at 2026-03-19T18:12:40Z. Monitoring: latency/err-ok, metric regressions present: longctx_recall_drop=0.024.

maya: Results from sam (on rtx-a6000): `--force-legacy-rotary` -> top5 0.881 (back to baseline). `--kvcache-stride 64` -> 0.879. So both knobs recover most of the loss.

aisha: That strongly points to combination of stride/prefill+rotary norm. Not purely quantization.

ravi: I pushed a quick rehydrate-check PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/7862 — it adds a debug endpoint `kv/check-snapshot` that compares live-phase vs snapshot-phase and emits a delta histogram. Can we run it on the failing snapshot?

maya: Running now on canary node, output gist: https://s3.redwood-internal/test-artifacts/deckchair-deltas-1759992345.json — summary: 97% tokens delta <1e-4, 3% between 1e-4 and 1e-2, tail beyond 1e-2 correlates with sparse prefill zones.

sam: Tail >1e-2 is worrying for longchain. Maybe accumulation error in int4 kernels is amplifying small phase diffs.

aisha: Next steps I propose:
1) run the rehydrate-check across a small set of snapshots (pre-refactor vs post-refactor) and collect delta histograms. (maya/qa)
2) run the repro with `--force-legacy-rotary` and `--kvcache-stride` sweeps to map sensitivity. (sam)
3) consider changing snapshot metadata to store high-precision rotary scale (float32) instead of quantized float16. (eng)
4) if reproducer shows it's definitely refactor, revert or gate the refactor behind `enable_prefill_normalization=false` until we have numeric parity tests. (product/eng)

ravi: I'll add a unit test that creates a small synthetic with wraparound indices and compares phases after snapshot/rehydrate across kernels. If int4 path deviates, we'll add a tolerance check.

maya: QA results: ran rehydrate-check across 5 snapshots — post-refactor snapshots show heavier tail in token delta. Putting artifact here: slack-repro/logs/1759992345/summary.txt

qa-bot: Automated regression job queued: `longctx-deckchair-smoke` on canary (3 runs). Link: https://ci.redwood-internal/longctx/1759992345

sam: Good. If we can get a short mitigation (store rotary_scale as float32 in snapshot) that might be low-lift. I can prototype that today.

maya: Thanks all. I'm going to pause further canary rollouts until we narrow root cause. Leaving notes in the onboarding checklist. :memo:

ravi: ping me if you want help bisecting the kvcache refactor commit range.

maya: Will do. I'll also add a small eval to nightly that compares prefill-phase histograms as a guardrail.

sam: Nice. Also let's avoid shipping poetic names like deckchair in prod snapshot IDs next time :stuck_out_tongue:
